title: Africa 2 of 8 · Atlantic West Africa
edition: Africa countries · Eight regional lessons · John · November 2026
intro: Welcome to Africa episode two of eight. First, I clear the chosen names for a fresh regional lesson.
Eight countries take us from offshore Cabo Verde down the Atlantic coast: Mauritania, Senegal, The Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea, Sierra Leone and Liberia.

states.name: Cabo Verde
lines: Cabo Verde is an Atlantic island country west of Senegal. Its islands sit offshore, separate from the mainland countries that follow the African coast.
Cidade Velha on Santiago preserves a fortress, churches and an early colonial street pattern. Its history connects these islands with Atlantic navigation and the exploitation of enslaved people.
Picture an old fortified town out in the Atlantic. Cabo Verde is the offshore stop west of Senegal, not a coastal province on the mainland.
states.transition: Let's bring Cabo Verde and its neighbours into view.

states.name: Mauritania
lines: Mauritania lies on the Atlantic below Western Sahara, north of Senegal and west of Mali. Much of the country belongs to the Sahara.
Desert towns including Chinguetti and Ouadane grew around caravan trade and Islamic learning. Their narrow streets and courtyard houses preserve the shape of Saharan trading settlements.
Picture a caravan town between desert routes and the Atlantic. Mauritania is above Senegal; Mali continues inland to its east.
states.transition: Let's bring Mauritania and its neighbours into view.

states.name: Senegal
lines: Senegal lies below Mauritania at Africa’s western shoulder. It surrounds The Gambia on land, while Guinea-Bissau and Guinea lie farther south.
Stone circles in Senegal and The Gambia form a shared archaeological landscape. Carefully shaped pillars and burial mounds record societies that built sacred monuments over many centuries.
Remember stone circles around the river country. Senegal wraps around The Gambia, so the long narrow shape inside its western side is a separate country.
states.transition: Let's bring Senegal and its neighbours into view.

states.name: The Gambia
lines: The Gambia is the narrow country following the River Gambia inland from the Atlantic. Senegal surrounds it on every landward side.
Kunta Kinteh Island and associated river sites preserve evidence of encounters between Africa and Europe, including the slave trade and its abolition. The river was a route into the interior.
Use the river as your memory line: a thin country inside Senegal. The Gambia reaches the Atlantic, although most of its outline looks like an inland ribbon.

states.name: Guinea-Bissau
lines: Guinea-Bissau lies below Senegal and northwest of Guinea. Its mainland coast faces the Atlantic, with the Bijagós islands just offshore.
The Bijagós archipelago has important coastal habitats and nesting beaches for sea turtles. Local communities and customary resource management are central to protecting this island environment.
Picture turtle islands off the small coast below Senegal. Guinea-Bissau is northwest of Guinea; their similar names belong to separate countries.
states.transition: Let's bring Guinea-Bissau and its neighbours into view.

states.name: Guinea
lines: Guinea lies below Guinea-Bissau and west of Mali, with Sierra Leone and Liberia to its south. Its territory reaches the Atlantic despite its broad inland part.
Mount Nimba rises near the meeting of Guinea, Liberia and Côte d'Ivoire. Its unusual wildlife includes a toad that gives birth to live young, rather than laying eggs in a pond.
Remember the live-bearing toad on the mountain border. Guinea is the larger inland-reaching country above Sierra Leone and Liberia, not Guinea-Bissau.

states.name: Sierra Leone
lines: Sierra Leone is the Atlantic country southwest of Guinea and northwest of Liberia. Its compact outline fits between those two neighbours.

The Gola-Tiwai protected landscape preserves Upper Guinean rainforest and river-island habitats. It shelters rare wildlife including the pygmy hippopotamus, a much smaller relative of the familiar river hippo.
Picture a small forest hippo in the compact coastal country. Sierra Leone comes before Liberia when following this coast southeast.

states.name: Liberia
lines: Liberia follows the Atlantic coast southeast of Sierra Leone, below Guinea and west of Côte d'Ivoire. Its inland forests connect with the wider Upper Guinean forest region.
Sapo National Park in Sinoe County protects an important tract of tropical forest. Liberia’s environmental authorities describe it as a major refuge for the country’s biodiversity.
Remember the forest refuge at the southeastern end of this coastal chain. Liberia lies between Sierra Leone and Côte d'Ivoire, not inland behind them.

recap: Cabo Verde is offshore. Mauritania lies above Senegal, which surrounds The Gambia on land. Guinea-Bissau is below Senegal, Guinea stretches inland, then Sierra Leone and Liberia follow the coast southeast.
Recall the old island town, caravan settlements, stone circles, river island, turtle beaches, live-bearing toad, pygmy hippo and forest refuge. Use the coastline to put the names back in order.
